functionalReqs: Display map tiles at any zoom level
Route from A to B by car, foot or bike
hints: Should the client download the raw map data or pre-rendered tiles? Which zoom levels?
Running Dijkstra on the whole world graph per request is too slow. How can you partition the graph?

Pre-rendered (or vector) tiles via CDN keyed by zoom/x/y; routing graph split into tiles with hierarchical routing (contraction hierarchies); live traffic from location pings aggregated per road segment by a stream processor; ETA service combining historical and live speeds.
nonFunctionalReqs: Routes computed in under a second
Smooth map rendering on mobile networks
problemStatement:
Design **Google Maps**: render maps, find routes between two points with ETAs that account for live traffic, and give turn-by-turn navigation.

The road network is a graph with hundreds of millions of edges.

scaleHints.qps: ~50K route requests/s; millions of location pings/s from navigating users
scaleHints.storage: Map tiles for every zoom level: petabytes

title: Design Google Maps
